I'm seeing a problem where invoking entire auth use --context xyz is returning a misleading error message. See this interaction:

❯ entire auth use --context eu.auth.entire.io
Usage:
  entire auth use <context> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for use

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Error: Invalid usage: accepts 1 arg(s), received 0

~/Development/entire on ☁️   entire 0.10.6-nightly@3d1b73ff2
❯ entire auth contexts
   CONTEXT             HANDLE        LOGIN SERVER
   us.auth.entire.io   matthiaswenz  https://us.auth.entire.io
*  eu.auth.entire.io   matthiaswenz  https://eu.auth.entire.io
   eu.auth.partial.to  matthiaswenz  https://eu.auth.partial.to

~/Development/entire on ☁️   entire 0.10.6-nightly@3d1b73ff2
❯ entire auth use --context eu.auth.entire.io
Usage:
  entire auth use <context> [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for use

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Error: Invalid usage: accepts 1 arg(s), received 0

so you can see how the first use of it returns an invalid usage though the arguments were provided.
it also did the job, i.e. the auth context got switched, but it still continues to claim it was a wrong request

look into if this is fixed in main, if anyone is working on it, and if not propose a change and push a trail to fix this
I'll start by understanding the bug, then check whether it's already fixed or being worked on.

input.content:
## What happens now

```
❯ entire auth use --context eu.auth.entire.io
Usage:
  entire auth use <context> [flags]
...
Error: Invalid usage: accepts 1 arg(s), received 0
```

The user typed an argument, so the message is about something they did not do.
Worse, it does not say that nothing was switched — reported as "it also did the
job, i.e. the auth context got switched, but it still continues to claim it was
a wrong request".

## Why it happens

`entire auth use` takes its context as a positional (`Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1)`).
The global `--context` flag, registered on the root in `context_flag.go`, takes a
context name too. Cobra therefore binds `eu.auth.entire.io` to the flag, no
positional is left, and `cobra.ExactArgs(1)` reports zero.

The two spellings mean nearly opposite things:

- `entire auth use NAME` writes `NAME` to `contexts.json` for every later command.
- `entire --context NAME ...` acts as `NAME` for the current invocation only —
  and on `auth use` it selects nothing at all, since switching the active context
  authenticates against nothing.

`--context` is the only global persistent flag on the root, and `auth use` is the
only command with a positional that collides with it, so this is a one-command
problem rather than a class of them.

## The active context was not switched

I could not reproduce a switch, and there is no code path for one:
`contextFlagValue.Set` only calls `contexts.SetFlagOverride`, which stores a
process-global `atomic.Pointer[string]` and writes nothing to disk. The command's
`RunE` — the only caller of `auth.SetCurrentContext` — never runs, because `Args`
fails first. Verified against an isolated `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR`: the active context
stays put across the failing command.

The likely explanation for what was observed is that `eu.auth.entire.io` was
already active before the first invocation — which is consistent with the
transcript, where both invocations fail identically and `auth contexts` shows
`*` on `eu` between them.

## The fix

`authUseArgs` answers the zero-positional-plus-`--context` case itself:

```
--context eu.auth.entire.io acts as that login for one command; it does not
switch the active context.
To switch, name the context as an argument:

  entire auth use eu.auth.entire.io
```

The message carries no `arg(s)`, so `main.isPositionalArgError` leaves the usage
dump off and prints it alone.

## What is deliberately left alone

The check is scoped to the zero-positional case. With a positional present,
`entire --context X auth use Y` still switches to `Y`: the flag is a no-op there,
and rejecting or warning about it would print noise for anyone whose shell alias
passes `--context` to every `entire` command. Flagging this rather than deciding
it — if you would rather it warn, say so and I will add it.

`ENTIRE_CONTEXT=NAME entire auth use` is the same class of mistake and is also
left alone: an exported `ENTIRE_CONTEXT` is a legitimate standing setting, so
reading it as the intended argument would mislead more often than it helped.

## Tests

Four tests in `auth_context_test.go`, all against a minimal cobra root that
registers the real `--context` flag:

- `TestAuthUse_ContextFlagInsteadOfArgument` — the new message names the flag,
  says it does not switch, shows the working command, and stays clear of
  `arg(s)`.
- `TestAuthUse_MissingArgumentKeepsArgCountError` — a bare `entire auth use`
  keeps cobra's error so the usage is still shown.
- `TestAuthUse_BlankContextFlagKeepsArgCountError` — `--context "  "` names
  nothing, so it falls through to the same.
- `TestAuthUseArgs_AcceptsNamedContextAlongsideFlag` — a named context plus the
  flag still validates.

`mise run check` is green (fmt, lint, `test:ci` including the Vogon canary).

Done. Trail: **https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1263** (branch `fix/auth-use-context-flag-collision`, commit `092aa8def`).

## Not fixed in main, nobody on it

- `origin/main` still has `Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1)` on `auth use`; last touches to `auth_context.go` / `context_flag.go` were unrelated (a docs fix, a trail-backend retirement).
- No open PR or issue about it, and no remote branch among the 80 most recent touches either file.

## Cause

`entire auth use` takes its context as a positional. The global `--context` flag (`context_flag.go`, the only persistent flag on the root) takes a context name too. So cobra binds `eu.auth.entire.io` to the flag, no positional is left, and `cobra.ExactArgs(1)` reports "received 0" about an argument you did type.

The two spellings mean nearly opposite things: `auth use NAME` writes `NAME` to `contexts.json` for good, while `--context NAME` acts as that login for one invocation — and on `auth use` it selects nothing at all, since switching the active context authenticates against nothing.

## One correction: the context did not switch

`contextFlagValue.Set` only calls `contexts.SetFlagOverride`, which stores a process-global pointer and writes nothing to disk. `auth.SetCurrentContext` is called only from `RunE`, which never ran — `Args` failed first. I reproduced against an isolated `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` and the active context stayed put.

`eu.auth.entire.io` was almost certainly already active before your first invocation — which fits the transcript: both invocations fail identically, and `auth contexts` shows `*` on `eu` between them.

## The change

`authUseArgs` answers that one case itself:

```
--context eu.auth.entire.io acts as that login for one command; it does not switch the active context.
To switch, name the context as an argument:

  entire auth use eu.auth.entire.io
```

No `arg(s)` in the text, so `main.isPositionalArgError` skips the usage dump and prints the message alone.

**Scoped to the zero-positional case on purpose.** `entire --context X auth use Y` still switches to `Y` — the flag is a no-op on a command that only writes `contexts.json`, and rejecting or warning would print noise for anyone whose shell alias passes `--context` to everything. That's a judgment call, called out in the trail; say the word if you'd rather it warn. `ENTIRE_CONTEXT=NAME entire auth use` is left alone for the same reason — an exported var is a standing setting, not a mistyped argument.

Four tests cover the new message, the bare `auth use` (keeps cobra's error and its usage), `--context "  "`, and the flag-plus-positional case. `mise run check` is green end to end — fmt, lint, and `test:ci` including the Vogon canary (exit 0, zero failures).
